sections.scope_note: Relists are read off the stored distribution count, which holds the `dist-v2` reading; a parse change moves which entries count as a relist, not the tier labels, so the parse travels with the numbers. The count is an upper bound on true relists under either reading — a reschedule before first consideration also adds a distribution entry.

sections.title: Cert petitions by CVSG status (paid scored segment)

buckets.key: (unknown)

sections.scope_note: Amicus briefs are counted at the petition's disposition — every docket entry before the first disposition entry, the same where-it-ended timing the relist cut reads off its stored count — so a granted case's merits amici are not counted. The per-entry reading is the interim amicus count's: each entry naming amicus or amici curiae, plus each distinct lead filer docketed as submitted and not yet accepted, less the Court's orders on amicus motions, so a brief filed by motion counts once. It is a stakes proxy, not a census of briefs: a multi-filer brief counts once, a paper reciting the phrase (a consent to amicus filings, a certificate of service on a brief) counts beside the briefs, and the Solicitor General's invited brief counts, so a CVSG petition whose invited brief is on the record sits at 1 or above by construction. `(unknown)` is a row the live poll has not read since the count was stored. The split is a marginal one — it describes the populations, not what the count adds over the relist and CVSG cuts.
sections.title: Cert petitions by amicus-brief count (paid scored segment)

buckets.key: unmarked
capital

sections.scope_note: The capital flag is latched from supremecourt.gov's own `bCapitalCase` payload field, OR-ed with the `*** CAPITAL CASE ***` annotation the same channel appends to the docket number — either alone under-reports, and no other channel serves either reading. So `last_live_polled` is the column's coverage sentinel: a row no live poll stamped buckets as `(unknown)` rather than as unmarked, and none appear here because this section is already scoped to the live slice, which is that stamp. Inside the slice the stamp records an attempted poll rather than an ingested payload, so `unmarked` means no channel that wrote the row read either signal — silence, not a denial. Read it as an upper bound: contamination runs one way, into `unmarked`, so it can only shrink the gap between these buckets, never widen it. The split is a marginal one — it describes what the two populations are, not what the marking adds over the cuts beside it.
sections.title: Cert petitions by capital-case marking (paid scored segment)
